title: Semrush’s New Topics Layer Helps Marketers Measure Brand Visibility Across Google and AI Search In One View
summary: 11/23/26 Semrush’s New Topics Layer Helps Marketers Measure Brand Visibility Across Google and AI Search In One View Topics combine Semrush’s 29B+ keywords and 317M+ AI prompts so marketers can see their visibility across a cluster of relevant queries. A new AI-influenced traffic metric shows how AI visibility converts into website visits. Ask any marketer today and they’ll tell you that growing brand visibility in AI search is top of mind. Yet most marketing teams right now are juggling keyword lists in one dashboard while tracking isolated AI prompts in another, which doubles the work and fragments reporting. Meanwhile, connected visibility growth happens at the topic level, where AI assistants evaluate trusted authority to make recommendations. To build lasting visibility for human searchers and AI engines alike, marketers should anchor their search strategy around whole topic clusters, instead of pursuing individual AI prompts or keywords alone. Semrush’s new Topics layer helps marketers optimize and measure their brand visibility across SEO and AI search in one connected view. It brings together Semrush’s expansive search intelligence of more than 29 billion keywords and over 317 million AI prompts so marketers can track how their brand performs across whole topics in Google and AI search, including ChatGPT, Gemini, AI Overviews and AI Mode. Plus, a new AI-influenced traffic metric in Semrush now helps marketers measure how visibility in AI answers leads to website visits later – a crucial piece to measuring the impact of their strategy. Until now, marketers have had to chase AI visibility one prompt at a time, separately from their SEO data. This disjointed view rarely gives the business a clear answer on how discoverable their brand is in AI platforms. By bringing SEO and AI search together at the topic level in Semrush, and introducing a new metric that estimates AI-influenced traffic, we’re helping teams see where to invest and prove the ROI of their brand visibility efforts. -Vitalii Obishchenko, VP, Software Development, Adobe One View Of Everything That Buyers Search and Ask The buyer journey is expanding, going far beyond a single search box. Buyers move between Google and AI assistants, and the results they see are increasingly personalized. A Semrush analysis found that U.S. users of major LLMs are spending about ten minutes per session in 2026, signifying a seismic shift in consumer behavior compared to traditional search. It also represents an opportunity for brands to find buyers where they’re searching, increasingly within AI platforms. Whether a brand gets recommended in AI search now depends on its relevance and authority across a whole topic, not its rank for one keyword or its mention in just one prompt. Marketers can use a topic to measure total search demand and competitive visibility across both search keywords and AI prompts, instead of relying on keyword volume alone. Plus, Topics brings both AI search and SEO data into one unified view, giving marketers a fuller picture of how their brand competes for visibility across search and AI. For example, a marketer for a skincare brand can track the topic ‘sensitive skincare’ to capture Google keywords like ‘moisturizer for sensitive skin’, as well as relevant AI prompts such as ‘what skincare routine works for my sensitive skin?’ Topics in Semrush reveals where the brand leads in Google, how it shows up in AI answers, and where its competitor compares across both. Semrush’s new Topics tool measures what matters to us now: how much of a topic we own, not where one keyword ranks. My team uses it for measurement, which is top of mind for leadership. And it’s also been a helpful tool for where we go next: content planning, internal linking and a whole lot more. -Rob Peck, Director of PPC and SEO, Mambo Media Finally, A Metric To Measure The Value Of AI Visibility Although most teams agree that AI search is important for brand discovery, marketers have struggled to demonstrate the return on their AI search efforts – until now. The new AI-influenced traffic metric estimates the traffic a brand gets when it’s mentioned or cited prominently in a topic’s AI answers, whether that traffic comes as direct visits, branded organic searches or AI referral clicks. It highlights traffic that standard analytics tools can’t currently attribute: visits that started with an AI recommendation rather than a search click. Semrush has also updated the way organic traffic from SERP position and search volume is estimated to reflect how click-through rates on Google have changed this year. The new CTR model takes more features of today’s SERPs into account, including search intent, branded versus non-branded keywords, SERP features, zero-click signals, and the impact of AI Overviews and AI Mode. The result is a more accurate estimate of the traffic a ranking position is likely to drive today. Availability The topics layer is rolling out across Semrush products from mid-November, starting with: Organic Rankings 2.0: A topic-level view of visibility across Google and AI search combined. It shows how fully a brand covers a topic compared to other industry players, and where AI systems are already citing competitors instead. Keyword Magic Tool 2.0: A redesigned keyword research tool with a new algorithm. It finds relevant keywords and prompts based on SERP and semantic similarity instead of keyword stemming, so they’re grouped by what they mean, not how they’re spelled. These reports are also available within Organic Rankings and Keyword & Prompt Research on the Semrush Enterprise platform. Topics will launch first in the US and UK, and then roll out to additional markets. Semrush plans to bring topic-level data and insights to more tools and reports, with more releases to follow. This unified view is also coming soon to Adobe Brand Visibility.

11/23/26


Semrush’s New Topics Layer Helps Marketers Measure Brand Visibility Across Google and AI Search In One View


Topics combine Semrush’s 29B+ keywords and 317M+ AI prompts so marketers can see their visibility across a cluster of relevant queries. A new AI-influenced traffic metric shows how AI visibility converts into website visits.


Ask any marketer today and they’ll tell you that growing brand visibility in AI search is top of mind. Yet most marketing teams right now are juggling keyword lists in one dashboard while tracking isolated AI prompts in another, which doubles the work and fragments reporting. Meanwhile, connected visibility growth happens at the topic level, where AI assistants evaluate trusted authority to make recommendations. To build lasting visibility for human searchers and AI engines alike, marketers should anchor their search strategy around whole topic clusters, instead of pursuing individual AI prompts or keywords alone.


Semrush’s new Topics layer helps marketers optimize and measure their brand visibility across SEO and AI search in one connected view. It brings together Semrush’s expansive search intelligence of more than 29 billion keywords and over 317 million AI prompts so marketers can track how their brand performs across whole topics in Google and AI search, including ChatGPT, Gemini, AI Overviews and AI Mode. Plus, a new AI-influenced traffic metric in Semrush now helps marketers measure how visibility in AI answers leads to website visits later – a crucial piece to measuring the impact of their strategy.


Until now, marketers have had to chase AI visibility one prompt at a time, separately from their SEO data. This disjointed view rarely gives the business a clear answer on how discoverable their brand is in AI platforms. By bringing SEO and AI search together at the topic level in Semrush, and introducing a new metric that estimates AI-influenced traffic, we’re helping teams see where to invest and prove the ROI of their brand visibility efforts.
-Vitalii Obishchenko, VP, Software Development, Adobe


One View Of Everything That Buyers Search and Ask


The buyer journey is expanding, going far beyond a single search box. Buyers move between Google and AI assistants, and the results they see are increasingly personalized. A Semrush analysis found that U.S. users of major LLMs are spending about ten minutes per session in 2026, signifying a seismic shift in consumer behavior compared to traditional search. It also represents an opportunity for brands to find buyers where they’re searching, increasingly within AI platforms.


Whether a brand gets recommended in AI search now depends on its relevance and authority across a whole topic, not its rank for one keyword or its mention in just one prompt. Marketers can use a topic to measure total search demand and competitive visibility across both search keywords and AI prompts, instead of relying on keyword volume alone. Plus, Topics brings both AI search and SEO data into one unified view, giving marketers a fuller picture of how their brand competes for visibility across search and AI.


For example, a marketer for a skincare brand can track the topic ‘sensitive skincare’ to capture Google keywords like ‘moisturizer for sensitive skin’, as well as relevant AI prompts such as ‘what skincare routine works for my sensitive skin?’ Topics in Semrush reveals where the brand leads in Google, how it shows up in AI answers, and where its competitor compares across both.


Semrush’s new Topics tool measures what matters to us now: how much of a topic we own, not where one keyword ranks. My team uses it for measurement, which is top of mind for leadership. And it’s also been a helpful tool for where we go next: content planning, internal linking and a whole lot more.
-Rob Peck, Director of PPC and SEO, Mambo Media


Finally, A Metric To Measure The Value Of AI Visibility


Although most teams agree that AI search is important for brand discovery, marketers have struggled to demonstrate the return on their AI search efforts – until now. The new AI-influenced traffic metric estimates the traffic a brand gets when it’s mentioned or cited prominently in a topic’s AI answers, whether that traffic comes as direct visits, branded organic searches or AI referral clicks. It highlights traffic that standard analytics tools can’t currently attribute: visits that started with an AI recommendation rather than a search click.


Semrush has also updated the way organic traffic from SERP position and search volume is estimated to reflect how click-through rates on Google have changed this year. The new CTR model takes more features of today’s SERPs into account, including search intent, branded versus non-branded keywords, SERP features, zero-click signals, and the impact of AI Overviews and AI Mode. The result is a more accurate estimate of the traffic a ranking position is likely to drive today.


Availability


The topics layer is rolling out across Semrush products from mid-November, starting with:


- **Organic Rankings 2.0:** A topic-level view of visibility across Google and AI search combined. It shows how fully a brand covers a topic compared to other industry players, and where AI systems are already citing competitors instead.
- **Keyword Magic Tool 2.0:** A redesigned keyword research tool with a new algorithm. It finds relevant keywords and prompts based on SERP and semantic similarity instead of keyword stemming, so they’re grouped by what they mean, not how they’re spelled.


These reports are also available within Organic Rankings and Keyword & Prompt Research on the Semrush Enterprise platform.


Topics will launch first in the US and UK, and then roll out to additional markets. Semrush plans to bring topic-level data and insights to more tools and reports, with more releases to follow. This unified view is also coming soon to Adobe Brand Visibility.
